advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the Verified +1 is attached to the current/rebased patchset SHA (not just present) before treating a member as fresh-verified.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:267: verified = (change.get("labels") or {}).get("Verified") or {}
infra/autolander/loop.py:268: if "approved" in verified:
docstring claim 'a present Verified +1 is by construction on the post-rebase SHA' — no code cross-checks the vote's patchset/SHA against wip.tested_shas
ticket AC: 'a Verified +1 on the exact rebased patchset SHA (not a copied/carried vote)'
advisory.finding: has_fresh_verified gates submit purely on the presence of a Verified +1 vote and never verifies the vote is attached to the recorded rebased SHA (wip.tested_shas[member_id]); its correctness rests entirely on an unvalidated assumption that Gerrit's copyCondition drops Verified on rebase. If that server config is wrong or changes, a carried/stale Verified vote passes the gate and the lander submits an untested tree — the exact R5 violation the ticket's AC ('a Verified +1 on the exact rebased patchset SHA (not a copied/carried vote)') calls out.
scenarios: Gerrit copyCondition misconfigured so Verified survives a trivial rebase
a member re-verified on an older patchset than the current one

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fetch each member once per poll and record the tested SHA from the same read that satisfied the fresh-verified gate.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:304: if all_members_fresh_verified(client, wip):
infra/autolander/loop.py:306: change = client.get_change(member_id, ["DETAILED_LABELS", "CURRENT_REVISION"])
all_members_fresh_verified already calls client.get_change per member at loop.py:280
advisory.finding: await_fresh_verified re-fetches every chain member a second time (loop at lines 305-310) after all_members_fresh_verified (line 304) already fetched each member. This doubles Gerrit reads per successful poll and opens a TOCTOU window: a member could receive a new patchset (dropping Verified) between the gate check and the recording loop, so the tested_shas/verified_at recorded may not correspond to the SHA that satisfied the gate.
scenarios: a new patchset lands on a member between the gate check and the record loop

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire drive_to_submit to call ancestor_atomic_submit so the partial-land safety guard is actually used on the live path.
evidence: infra/autolander/loop.py:227: client.submit(wip.change_id)
ancestor_atomic_submit defined at loop.py:317 but no in-package caller (search for 'ancestor_atomic_submit' returns only the definition)
drive_to_submit docstring: 'submit (ancestor-atomic; S2c refines the submit call)'
advisory.finding: The new ancestor_atomic_submit (with its mandatory partial-land safety) is not wired into the existing drive_to_submit path, which still calls client.submit(wip.change_id) directly at line 227 with no post-submit MERGED verification. As added, the loud PartialLandError guard is unreachable from the actual drive loop, so a partial land in production would go undetected via the live path.
scenarios: a real partial land occurs while drive_to_submit performs the bare submit

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm all existing change_info callers still behave with the new default args and parameterized status.
evidence: tests/autolander/_fakes.py:20: autosubmit_date: str | None = None,
tests/autolander/_fakes.py:24: status: str = "NEW",
diff removed hard-coded 'status': 'NEW' in favor of the parameter
advisory.finding: change_info's signature changed: autosubmit_date lost its required-positional status (now defaults to None) and the new status parameter defaults to 'NEW' but the returned dict's 'status' now derives from it rather than the previous hard-coded 'NEW'. Existing tests/callers that passed autosubmit_date positionally still work, but any caller relying on the old keyword-only-without-default contract or asserting a fixed status should be re-checked.
scenarios: other autolander tests constructing change_info without autosubmit_date

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert await_fresh_verified's success path populates wip.tested_shas and wip.verified_at for every member (not just the boolean return).
evidence: Impl records observable state on success: `wip.tested_shas[member_id] = change.get("current_revision")` and `wip.verified_at[member_id] = approved.get("date") or time_fn()` (infra/autolander/loop.py:307-310)
Docstring guarantees this: 'Poll until EVERY member carries a fresh Verified +1 (recording the tested SHA + verified timestamp on wip)' (infra/autolander/loop.py:295-296)
test_await_returns_true_when_all_fresh asserts only `assert got is True` (tests/autolander/test_s2c_submit_held_out.py:62) — no assertion on wip.tested_shas / wip.verified_at

Regression relevance: is_landable compares the freshly-recorded tested_shas against current_revision (infra/autolander/loop.py:179), so a broken recording in await would silently break the pre-submit TOCTOU check while all S2c tests stay green
advisory.finding: await_fresh_verified's documented success-path side effects — recording each member's tested SHA into wip.tested_shas and the verified timestamp into wip.verified_at — are asserted by no test; the True-path test (test_await_returns_true_when_all_fresh) checks only the boolean return.
scenarios: A refactor that stops updating wip.tested_shas (or records the wrong key) inside await_fresh_verified passes every test yet corrupts the downstream is_landable check

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a has_fresh_verified case with an 'all' entry value>=1 and no 'approved' key to cover the fallback branch.
evidence: Impl has a distinct branch: `for entry in verified.get("all") or []: if (entry.get("value") or 0) >= 1: return True` (infra/autolander/loop.py:270-272)

change_info(verified=True) always sets `labels["Verified"]["approved"]`, so `if "approved" in verified: return True` short-circuits (tests/autolander/_fakes.py:36-38) — the 'all'-scan branch is never reached in any test
test_has_fresh_verified_reads_current_patchset_vote only covers verified=True (approved present) and verified=False (value 0) (tests/autolander/test_s2c_submit_held_out.py:105-106)
advisory.finding: has_fresh_verified's non-'approved' branch (Verified label with an 'all' entry of value>=1 but no top-level 'approved' key) is never exercised; the fake always emits 'approved' whenever verified=True.
scenarios: Gerrit returns a Verified +1 in labels.Verified.all without a summarized 'approved' object; the fallback branch would need to fire but is untested
